title: Mirabel and the Promise
premise: Mirabel Halloran, a lighthouse keeper's granddaughter scraping out a living as a part-time novelist, has spent twenty years rebuilding herself after a fire that took her family's home and nearly took her life — a life measured in small, safe steps. For a decade she has corresponded with 'D. Halloran,' a stranger whose letters became her lifeline; when he finally moves in next door, she discovers Dominic is not only real but the very firefighter who pulled her from the flames, writing under a borrowed name out of guilt. As their friendship deepens into love, Dominic's career hangs on a promotion requiring him to testify in a lawsuit that would paint the fire as Mirabel's own negligence — a lie that would shatter her fragile identity. In the end, Dominic sacrifices the career that saved him to tell the truth, and Mirabel must decide whether the woman she has become can survive being fully seen; they choose each other, lighting the restored lighthouse together.
about_author: Lena Iversen is a former coastal archivist who spent five years cataloguing lighthouse logs before turning to fiction full time. She writes from a converted boathouse on the northern Atlantic coast, where the weather does half her editing for her.

chapters.title: The Keeper's Granddaughter
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Twenty years after the fire, Mirabel tends the decommissioned lighthouse cottage, teaches part-time, and writes forgettable romance novels under a pen name. Her ritual of rereading ten years of letters from 'D. Halloran' establishes her one unguarded connection. Beat: quiet loneliness disguised as contentment.

chapters.title: Letters to a Stranger
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. A decorated fire captain on medical leave after a rescue gone wrong, Dominic confesses in flashback why he began writing to the girl he saved: guilt over the three minutes he hesitated at the door. He accepts a transfer to the coastal town where she lives. Beat: dread braided with longing.

chapters.title: The New Neighbor
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. A moving truck arrives next door; Mirabel meets Dominic without recognizing him, though something about his voice snags like a splinter. She offers bread and boundaries. That night she writes him a letter about the neighbor, laughing at the coincidence. Beat: unease beneath charm.

chapters.title: What the Fire Left
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Dominic unpacks boxes containing his letters' drafts and the official incident report he was never supposed to keep. He watches Mirabel through the hedge, unable to reveal himself, terrified the truth will cost her the stability she's built. Beat: guilt tightening its grip.

chapters.title: Small Safe Steps
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. A town festival forces proximity; Dominic walks her home along the cliff path when fog rolls in, and his calm competence in the dark unsettles her — how does he know this path so well? First flicker of attraction. Beat: warmth shadowed by instinctive suspicion.

chapters.title: The Promotion
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. His chief offers him the captaincy permanently — contingent on testimony in an insurance lawsuit claiming the Halloran fire was caused by the family's own negligence. The department needs a scapegoat; Dominic is their star witness. Beat: ambition colliding with conscience.

chapters.title: Reading Between Lines
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Rereading old letters, Mirabel notices details 'D.' shouldn't know — the smell of smoke in her hair, the exact color of her childhood blanket. She begins a private investigation into her correspondent while falling harder for the neighbor. Beat: curiosity sharpening into alarm.

chapters.title: Two Names, One Man
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Mirabel invites him to dinner; halfway through, she quotes one of his letters verbatim, watching his face. He deflects, barely. Alone afterward he drafts a confession and burns it in the sink. Beat: the mask slipping, terror of exposure.

chapters.title: The Archive Room
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. In the county records office, Mirabel pulls the fire report and finds a firefighter's name redacted but a signature she almost recognizes. An archivist mentions a young firefighter who requested the file twice last year. Beat: the past reaching forward.

chapters.title: Almost
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. A near-miss: Mirabel finds his draft letters in a box he lends her for book research. He claims they're fiction. She believes him — or chooses to — and kisses him for the first time. Beat: love arriving precisely when honesty becomes impossible.

chapters.title: The Summons
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Mirabel is served: she is named in the insurance suit as the negligent party. Her safe life cracks open publicly; neighbors whisper, her editor wants a tell-all memoir instead of her novel. Beat: the price of survival coming due.

chapters.title: What He Knows
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Dominic realizes the department expects him to perjure himself against the woman he loves. His chief hints that refusal ends his career and blacklists him. He visits the burned ruin of the Halloran house at night. Beat: the choice taking shape.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Cliff Edge
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Mirabel confronts Dominic with everything — the letters, the file request, the way he knew the path. He admits he is D. Halloran but hides the worst: that he was inside the house that night and hesitated. Feeling betrayed by the half-truth, she sends him away. Beat: heartbreak as revelation.

chapters.title: Twenty Years Ago
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, flashback chapter. The night of the fire rendered whole: young Mirabel trapped upstairs, young Dominic frozen at the threshold before going in, the burns on his hands he's always explained away. Beat: compassion replacing anger as the full truth surfaces for the reader.

chapters.title: The Deposition
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Under oath, Dominic testifies — truthfully — that the fire was electrical, the family blameless, and that response delays were the department's own. The room detonates. His chief promises ruin. Beat: the climax of conscience; the career that saved him begins to burn.

chapters.title: Fallout
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. News of Dominic's testimony reaches Mirabel secondhand. The suit collapses, but her identity crisis peaks: if the fire wasn't her fault, who has she been all these years, building walls around a crime she never committed? Beat: grief and liberation tangled.

chapters.title: The Empty House Next Door
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Dominic packs to leave, suspended and disgraced. Mirabel finds his unsent final letter — twenty pages confessing everything, ending with 'you were never the one who needed saving.' She runs through the rain to the ferry dock. Beat: desperation turned to hope.

chapters.title: Seen at Last
chapters.summary: Both POVs converge. On the dock, Mirabel tells Dominic she doesn't want the man who saved her; she wants the man who wrote to her for ten years and finally told the truth. They say the things the letters never dared. Beat: emotional climax; love chosen over safety.

chapters.title: Rebuilding
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Weeks later: the lawsuit settled, Dominic working volunteer rescue while appealing his suspension. Together they begin restoring the lighthouse lamp room, Mirabel's hands steady for the first time. She starts a new novel — a true one. Beat: healing as active work, not miracle.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The disciplinary board rules; Mirabel speaks on his behalf, reading aloud the first letter he ever sent her. He is reinstated at reduced rank — enough. Walking out, he cares less about the badge than the hand holding his. Beat: justice tempered, priorities reordered.

chapters.title: Lighting the Lamp
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The restored lighthouse is relit in a small ceremony; the town that whispered now applauds. Mirabel reads the dedication from her finished novel, which she signs with her real name for the first time. Beat: identity reclaimed; the beacon as metaphor made literal.

chapters.title: The Promise
chapters.summary: Epilogue, alternating voices. One year on: two houses joined by an open gate, a wedding planned for spring, a new letter — this one hand-delivered, beginning 'Dear Mirabel' and signed with his true name. The last line mirrors the first letter he ever wrote. Beat: full-circle peace; loyalty and truth finally the same thing.
